reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first four premises by demonstrating full densification, grain refinement, high dislocation density, and enhanced mechanical properties in ZrB2 via UHPS at 1450 °C and 15 GPa. However, the fifth premise regarding resistance to liquid plating bath degradation is not addressed by the cited evidence, representing a significant gap in support.
premises: UHPS can fully densify ZrB2 at a reduced temperature (e.g., 1450 °C vs. >2300 °C)
UHPS produces a refined grain size and high dislocation density in ZrB2
The refined microstructure and high dislocation density enhance mechanical properties (hardness, fracture toughness)
The enhanced plastic deformation and dislocation multiplication are the dominant densification mechanisms under UHPS
The improved microstructure will reduce pore formation and increase resistance to degradation in a liquid plating bath
